text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Christian Democrats' employee lobby group calls for new "solidarity pact" between government, employers and workers
- Parliamentary parties fail to agree on reform of parliament
- German industry sees good opportunities in Latin America
- Upper House calls on Bonn to limit banks' power
- Environment Minister to introduce new plan for recycling of packaging
HANDELSBLATT
- With austerity package passed, Bonn government already considering new savings measures
- Veba and Ruhrgas agree telecommunications link-up
- Transport ministry says motorway fee for private cars would not pay
- RWE boss says Germany losing ground in global markets
- VW goes to European Court in subsidy row
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Centrist liberal FDP members of parliament fail to accept government draft of new bill expanding police surveillance powers
- Health minister says citizens must pay more for health care
- Catholics call on state to rediscover solidarity with poorer members of society
- Deutsche Telekom to devote more effort to marketing pay-TV
DIE WELT
- Low turnout in local election in Lower Saxony state
- Bonn ruling coalition plans new savings programme
- German firms being investigated for supplying arms to Iraq, magazine says
- Veba launches telecommunications cooperation with gas industry
- Education minister Ruettgers fears new shortfall of training places for school leavers in 1997
- German farmers demand more money from EU
- Union leaders threaten strikes to prevent employers revising existing labour contracts to cut sick pay
- FDP still pressing for early tax reform
- Deutsche Bank seeks new boss for Morgan Grenfell Asset Management
